Only three conversion functions are tested; adding Kelvin-to-Celsius or Fahrenheit-to-Kelvin would round out TDD practice without raising difficulty.
No significant weaknesses; the hints on recursive descent structure and right-associativity make this an exceptionally well-designed hard kata.

Difficulty leans toward upper-medium rather than hard since the hints fully prescribe the architecture (three-function recursive descent + token array), leaving little design exploration for the practitioner.
No significant weaknesses; the kata is well-scoped with clear requirements, correct and concrete tests, appropriate medium complexity, and natural TDD progression.
No significant weaknesses; all requirements map directly to tests and the kata cleanly exercises incremental TDD with meaningful business rules.
No significant weaknesses; requirements, tests, and difficulty are well-balanced for a beginner TDD exercise.
The kata is well-constructed but the 'custom rules' in the title implies configurability that the requirements don't deliver, creating a minor expectation mismatch.
Slightly leans easy for medium since all discount logic is straightforward conditionals with no edge cases around floating-point rounding or promo stacking order ambiguity.
Slightly leans easy for experienced developers but the statement formatting and aggregate tracking make it well-rounded for intermediate TDD practice.
Difficulty leans medium rather than easy — six requirements with two discount stacking rules and edge cases exceed a typical 30-minute beginner kata.
exampleTest covers only 3 of the 5 requirements — empty local part and TLD length (2-6 chars) have no example assertions, leaving learners without a test-first anchor for those rules.
The example test does not cover nested function calls or negative numbers despite both being listed as requirements, leaving those edge cases unverified.
Circular structure handling requirement lacks a testable example, leaving implementors guessing between cycle detection and depth limits.
Requirements lack explicit handling of edge cases like coupon exceeding subtotal or discount order ambiguity when both member discount and coupon are applied simultaneously.
No significant weaknesses; requirements are complete, the example test is syntactically valid and semantically consistent, complexity is well-calibrated for 60-minute TDD practice.
Case-insensitive vowel handling is mentioned in requirements but not tested with mixed-case examples, leaving an ambiguity gap.
No significant weaknesses; all dimensions are well-executed for a beginner kata.

exampleTest is semantically broken: 5 Apples + 12 Oranges at 2.00 with 10% bulk discount = 5.00 + 21.60 = 26.60 subtotal after discounts, not 29.00; and the promo/tax math (26.60 × 0.9 × 1.08 ≠ 25.68) is also inconsistent, making the example test actively misleading for TDD.
No significant weaknesses; this is a well-structured classic kata with clear incremental requirements ideal for TDD practice.
